items.title: Data Centers Must Disclose Erratic Power Use, Regulators Say
items.summary: As the data centers powering the AI boom grow larger and more numerous, they pose increasing challenges to the grid. Single facilities can draw as much power as a large city and their demand can lurch by hundreds of megawatts in seconds, straining the power grid . To rein in these wild electricity swings, U.S. regulators are beginning to write new rules. Their first step: Requiring data centers to disclose how their facilities interact with the grid, and just how wild their power swings are. To that end, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), an international regulatory authority, in October adopted its first reliability standards for computational loads.
